biggest_catch: The $95 annual fee is charged in year one, so the real first-year value is $300 minus $95 = $205 in cash redemption — and only if you meet the $1,500 spend with purchases you were already going to make.
catches: Never spend extra solely to chase the $1,500 threshold — only use spending you already planned (groceries, bills, gas).
The $95 annual fee is charged in year one, so the net first-year bonus value is about $205 after the fee, not $300.
Applying involves a hard credit inquiry; Truist will pull your credit report when you apply.
Carrying a balance at 18.74%–27.74% variable APR can erase the bonus many times over — pay the balance in full every month.

Bonus requires the account to be open and in good standing; points expire 5 years after issuance; cash redemptions have a $25 minimum and can take until after the close of the billing period in which rewards were earned.
Balance transfers, cash advances, fees, and gift-card/quasi-cash purchases do not count as eligible purchases toward the $1,500 threshold.

steps: Open the official Truist page https://www.truist.com/credit-cards/enjoy-beyond and start the application — do not apply from an affiliate link that shows different terms.
Complete the application with your identity, income, and SSN/ITIN; Truist runs a hard credit inquiry when you apply.
If approved, spend $1,500 on purchases you were already planning within the first 90 days of account opening (about $500/month of normal spending).
Pay the balance in full every month — carrying a balance at 18.74%–27.74% variable APR destroys the bonus.
After the spend threshold is met, the 30,000 bonus points post to your rewards account; redeem them for cash (statement credit, deposit to a Truist account, or check) at 1¢ per point = $300.
timing: Application takes 20–40 min active; then spend $1,500 in already-planned purchases within 90 days; bonus points post after the threshold is met and are redeemable after the close of that billing period (account in good standing).
